gloss: no matter what; at all costs; by any means

definitions.gloss: no matter what; at all costs; by any means
definitions.explanation: Expresses strong determination to achieve something regardless of obstacles or difficulty.

examples.japanese: {何|なん}としても{合格|ごうかく}したい。
examples.english: I want to pass no matter what.

examples.japanese: {何|なん}としても{明日|あした}までに{終|お}わらせなければならない。
examples.english: I must finish this by tomorrow no matter what.

examples.japanese: チームは{何|なん}としても{優勝|ゆうしょう}するという{強|つよ}い{気持|きも}ちで{試合|しあい}に{臨|のぞ}んだ。
examples.english: The team went into the match with a strong determination to win the championship at all costs.

notes:
USAGE:
Expresses strong resolve or urgency. Often followed by verbs expressing desire (～たい) or obligation (～なければならない). Similar in meaning to {是|ぜ}が{非|ひ}でも but more colloquial.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {何|なん}としても{成功|せいこう}させる (to make it succeed no matter what)
- {何|なん}としても{守|まも}る (to protect at all costs)
- {何|なん}としてでも (even stronger variant with でも)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- どうしても: no matter what — similar meaning but slightly less emphatic
- {是|ぜ}が{非|ひ}でも: by all means — more literary and formal
